question: does the judge reliability measured on the variance block replicate on the new confirmation tasks
design: all 48 element judgements over the 8 first-repeat confirmation artifacts, each judged independently by two models from different provider families

comparison_with_earlier_block.reading: raw agreement is lower on the new tasks, 0.667 against 0.703, because six items produced an unparsed verdict from one judge and are counted as disagreements. Excluding those, agreement is 0.788 with kappa 0.492, above the earlier 0.703 and 0.411. The important result is the stratification: every one of the twelve items where both judges were above 0.9 agreed, and none of the nine below 0.7 did.

what_this_supports: the confidence floor, which is the part of the instrument that is actually used, held on unseen tasks
what_this_does_not_support: a claim that the judge is reliable in general; below the floor the two judges disagree on about a third of items
limits: the same prompt and span retrieval for both judges, so a shared retrieval failure would look like agreement
six of thirty-nine items produced an unparsed verdict from at least one judge, which is counted as a disagreement rather than dropped
claim_scope: instrument reliability evidence only; no episode is scored here
headline: the stratified structure replicated exactly: perfect agreement above 0.9 confidence, 0.778 in the middle band, and zero below 0.7, which is the same shape measured on the variance block and on the replay of recorded verdicts
